title: Photo Gallery & Carousel
prompt: Design a reusable responsive photo gallery with a full-screen lightbox and carousel navigation. Metadata and image variants come from a server. Focus on image loading, layout stability, keyboard use and cleanup after long browsing. Draw the component/data-flow architecture, define state owners and contracts, and explain performance, accessibility and recovery. No UI coding is required.
functionalReqs: Render responsive thumbnails with stable aspect ratios
Open a deep-linkable lightbox and move next/previous
Support loading/error fallback, touch and keyboard controls
nonFunctionalReqs: 2,000 metadata entries; fetch 30 thumbnails/page; lightbox prefetch only previous/next.
Use meaningful alt text, keyboard next/previous, an accessible modal with Escape, trapped focus and focus restoration to the opened thumbnail; respect reduced motion.
Keep thumbnail/placeholder, expose retry, ignore old selection loads, abort expendable prefetch and revoke local object URLs.

scale.notes: 2,000 metadata entries; fetch 30 thumbnails/page; lightbox prefetch only previous/next.
scale.storage: 1,600 × 900 decoded image × 4 bytes/pixel; illustrative interview assumptions, not measured guarantees.

outOfScope: Backend sharding, ranking algorithms and infrastructure provisioning
Implementing a production UI inside this exercise
deepDives: Use responsive image sizes with intrinsic width/height; lazy-load below-fold thumbnails and preload at most adjacent lightbox images. Keep the selected photo by stable ID; do not automatically advance a carousel without pause and user control.
A full-resolution image fails while navigating quickly
A static grid is simpler and avoids modal navigation complexity. Preloading all full-resolution photos is wasteful even if metadata is small.
